<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par110 />express the distinct assurance or promise that an action or state will ensue as the certain consequence of a previous action. So especially:

(''a'') The imperative when depending (with {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}) upon another imperative. In this case the first imperative contains, as a rule, a condition, while the second declares the consequence which the fulfilment of the condition will involve. The imperative is used for this declaration, since the consequence is, as a matter of fact, intended or desired by the speaker (cf. ''divide et impera''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת עֲשׂוּ וִֽחְיוּ|translate=this do, and live}}, i.e. thus shall ye continue to live. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=22|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְהִוָּֽשְׁעוּ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=4}}, 6, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=3}}f., 4:4, 7:2, 13:20 {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=20|verse=20}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=נָא}} is added to the first imperative. In other cases, the first imperative contains a mocking concession, the second an irrevocable denunciation, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫עוּ עַמִּים וָחֹ֫תּוּ}} (continue to) ''make an uproar, O ye peoples, and ye shall be broken in pieces''; cf. verse 9 ''b''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|110|g}}
Rem. 1. If a promise or threat dependent on an imperative be expressed in the 3rd pers. then the jussive is naturally used instead of the 2nd imperative {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=2|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|110|h}}
2. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=13}} the second imperative (containing a promise) is attached by asyndeton; elsewhere two imperatives occur side by side without the copula, where the second might be expected to be subordinated to the first, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=הָחֵל רָשׁ}} (where {{GHGheb|text=רָשׁ}} is virtually, as it were, an object to {{GHGheb|text=הָחֵל}}) ''begin, take in possession'' for ''to take in possession'' (cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹאֶל־נָא וְלִין|translate=be content, I pray thee, and tarry all night}}, and on this kind of co-ordination in general, cf. {{GHGpar|120|d}}). But such imperatives as {{GHGheb|text=(לְכוּ) לֵךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=(ק֫וּמוּ) קוּם}}, when immediately preceding a second imperative, are for the most part only equivalent to interjections, ''come! up!''

{{GHGmargin-letter|110|i}}
(''b'') The imperative, when depending (with {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}) upon a jussive (cohortative), or an interrogative sentence, frequently expresses also a consequence which is to be expected with certainty, and often a consequence which is intended, or in fact an intention; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=7}} ''and he shall pray for thee'', {{GHGheb|text=וֶחְֽיֵה|translate=and thou shalt live}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=128|verse=5}} ''the Lord bless thee ... so that'' (or ''in order that'') ''thou seest'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=11|hidebook=1}}; after a cohortative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהוֹצֵא|translate=that thou mayest bring forth}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=12}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=35|verse=15}} (after imperative and jussive); after an interrogative sentence, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=3}} ''wherewith shall I make atonement'', {{GHGheb|text=וּבָֽרֲכוּ|translate=that ye may bless}}, &c.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=19}} the imperative without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} (in 32:23 with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}) is used after a conditional clause in the sense of a definite promise.

{{GHGmargin-letter|110|k}}
Rem. The ''2nd sing. masc.'' occurs in addressing feminine persons in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}} ({{GHGheb|text=עֲמֹד}}, according to Qimḥi an infinitive, in which case, however, the infinitive absolute {{GHGheb|text=עָמֹד}} should be read; but probably we should simply read {{GHGheb|text=עִמְדִי}} with Moore), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=13}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=13|verse=7}} (after {{GHGheb|text=עוּרִי}}); and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=1}}, the ''2nd plur. masc.'' (On<section end=par110 /><noinclude>
